title: Inspect identities and content of selected engineering subjects
description: Compute exact byte identities for explicitly selected safe engineering subjects and optionally return those same inspected bytes. This supplies observation for an actor's declared decision basis; it neither chooses subjects nor refreshes the basis during a later write.
inputs: Explicit repository root and distinct contained subject paths.
Requested identity-only or full-content mode and allowed response budget.
outputs: One coherent observed subject set with path and byte identity, plus the same inspected content when requested.
Explicit expected absence or a safe path, read, limit, or observed-change failure.
behavior: Inspect only supplied paths under the published containment and subject-count rules; do not execute content or infer dependencies from a stage.
Compute identity from the same observed bytes returned as content; identity-only inspection need not retain full payloads.
Represent a missing subject with explicit absence and observation, usable as an expected-absence read rather than a non-null stored Subject.
Return declared identities for explicit later use; a mutation must check those supplied identities without silently rereading and replacing the actor's expectation.

failure_behavior.condition: An observed subject change prevents a coherent identity/content result.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return conflict without a partial subject set, retaining the published observed-check limitation for outside edits.

failure_behavior.condition: A path is unsafe, nonregular, symlinked, unreadable, or too large for requested full output.
failure_behavior.outcome: Reject safely without truncation, execution, or undisclosed content; identity-only use does not itself establish sufficient engineering context.

sources.basis: Functional Analysis of the IR-008 system obligations confirms this distinct published command/record responsibility. The retained CLI/Record Format contract supplies exact public operations and limits; logical behavior is defined before Module allocation.

Assign MOD-011 as the proposed accountable primary responsibility after Functional Analysis. Current product source contracts retain detailed behavior authority; allocation is not runtime adoption or complete AR coverage.
